image.prompt:
Straight-on ELEVATION photograph of one whole high-rise building, taken from very far away with a long telephoto lens: the camera is level with the building's mid-height, so every vertical edge is perfectly vertical and parallel with no keystone convergence, and the main facade is seen frontally with only a thin sliver of one side. Not a three-quarter view, not an aerial view, not looking up from the street.

The building: Modern forty-storey luxury condominium tower, white rendered slab edges with continuous full-height grey tinted glass, tall vertical white aluminium fins on the long facade, cantilevered corner balconies with frosted glass balustrades stacked to the top, a rooftop infinity pool deck with a slatted timber screen and a double-height glazed lobby at the base Materials: clean white render and white aluminium fins, dark grey tinted glass, frosted glass balustrades, timber-look aluminium slats.

Whole building: the complete tower from its ground-floor base to the very top of its crown, roof plant, spire or antenna, with nothing cropped. The base sits at the bottom of the silhouette with nothing in front of it: no trees, no street, no cars, no people, no neighbouring buildings, no scaffolding. The only text is lettering explicitly described above; otherwise no signs, no logos, no watermarks, no annotations.

Framing: the building is centred and fills about 85% of the frame along its longer axis, with a clear empty margin on every side.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080) fills every part of the frame that is not the building, including where the sky would be and where the ground would be. The building is a cut-out floating against an infinite flat backdrop. No sky, no clouds, no horizon, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient, no haze, no atmospheric fade.

Lighting: bright overcast daylight, flat and even, soft and shadowless, so the facade reads as true albedo with its glass tint, concrete and paint colours exactly as described. No sun glare, no specular blowout, no lens flare, no dramatic sky colour reflected in the glass.

One building only. Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, every floor, window, mullion and balcony resolved, realistic weathering and grime. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render, not a wireframe, not low-poly.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Glass-Fin Condo Tower
nameTh: คอนโดกระจกครีบ
notes: The bright, clean tower of the batch and a foil to the beige and grey ones; the white fin rhythm has to resolve as individual fins at 2K, so they must not be painted as a single striped texture. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 9:16, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand. Width corrected from the plate on 2026-08-27: keyed silhouette aspect 0.392 x declared height 150 m = 58.8 m against the listed 40 m (47% off); the quad carries the plate at true height so its width must follow the plate or the texture stretches.
